chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about regurgitation, does it break the fast of the fasting person? He (peace be upon him) said: No.
ai.seo_question: Does regurgitation (qals) break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that *qals*—the regurgitation of vomit that returns to the throat and is swallowed—does not invalidate the fast, distinguishing it from full vomiting which is generally considered to break the fast in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle that the fast is only broken by the deliberate swallowing of the entire mass of vomit, emphasizing the distinction between involuntary regurgitation and intentional consumption. The narration underscores the ease (*taysir*) in Shia fiqh, ensuring that minor physiological occurrences do not unduly burden the fasting individual.
